o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish وِیرْكُو (vergü), from Proto-Turkic *bērgi. By surface analysis, ver- (“to give”) + -gi.

Probably from Persian سوهان (suhân).
For the final /d/ absent in the etymon, compare Persian آسان (âsân, “easy”) giving the colloquial Azerbaijani byform asand, along with the standard asan.
From Proto-Common Turkic *bōnčuk, from Proto-Common Turkic *bōyïn-čuk, from Proto-Turkic *bōyïn (“neck”).
Calque of Russian соверше́нно секре́тный (soveršénno sekrétnyj, literally “completely secret”).
